senses.gloss: To tell someone about your thoughts, feelings, or news.
examples: Thanks for *sharing* your story with us.
She *shared* the news with her family first.
He never *shares* what he is feeling.

senses.gloss: To make something clearer, stronger, or more effective.
examples: A year abroad will *sharpen* your Spanish.
The debate *sharpened* the differences between the two sides.
Competition has *sharpened* the company's focus on price.

senses.gloss: To destroy someone's hopes, confidence, or peace of mind.
examples: The injury *shattered* his hopes of playing again.
News like that can *shatter* a family.
Her confidence was completely *shattered* by the experience.

senses.gloss: To decide not to continue with a plan or project, at least for now.
senses.ru: откладывать, отложить (проект, план); класть под сукно
examples: The city *shelved* plans for a new stadium.
If the funding falls through, they will *shelve* the whole project.
The bill has been *shelved* until after the election.

senses.gloss: To move blame, cost, or responsibility onto someone else.
examples: Don't try to *shift* the blame onto me.
The new rules *shifted* the cost to employers.
The company has *shifted* responsibility for repairs to the tenants.

senses.gloss: To give someone a painful jolt of electricity.
examples: Don't touch that wire, or it will *shock* you.
A frayed cord *shocked* him when he plugged it in.
Two workers were *shocked* by a live cable.

senses.gloss: To lift something onto your shoulder and carry it.
senses.ru: взваливать на плечо, взвалить; нести на плече
examples: He *shouldered* his pack and started up the trail.
Two firefighters *shouldered* the ladder.
She was *shouldering* a heavy duffel bag.

senses.gloss: To push someone or something with your shoulder.
examples: He *shouldered* his way through the crowd.
A reporter *shouldered* past us to reach the door.
Don't *shoulder* people out of the line.

senses.gloss: To wash yourself under a shower.
senses.ru: принимать душ, принять душ; мыться под душем
examples: I *shower* every morning before work.
She *showered* and changed before dinner.
He was *showering* when the phone rang.

senses.gloss: To walk slowly without lifting your feet properly off the ground.
examples: The old man *shuffled* to the door in his slippers.
Patients *shuffle* up and down the hallway for exercise.
She was *shuffling* around the kitchen at six in the morning.

senses.gloss: To close the shutters over a window.
examples: They *shuttered* the windows before the hurricane.
*Shutter* the windows on the north side too.
The beach houses stood *shuttered* all winter.

senses.gloss: To go through a large amount of material carefully in order to find something.
examples: Investigators *sifted* the wreckage for clues.
We are still *sifting* hundreds of applications.
The committee has *sifted* every document in the file.

senses.gloss: To communicate using sign language.
senses.ru: говорить на языке жестов, показывать жестами
examples: Both of her parents are deaf, so she *signs* fluently.
An interpreter *signed* the whole ceremony.
He was *signing* to a friend across the room.

senses.gloss: To hire a player or performer by getting them to sign a contract.
senses.ru: подписывать контракт с (кем-л.), нанимать по контракту
examples: The team *signed* a new quarterback in March.
The label wants to *sign* her before anyone else does.
They have *signed* him for three more years.

senses.gloss: To show clearly that something is true or is going to happen.
senses.ru: свидетельствовать о, сигнализировать (о намерении); давать понять
examples: The decision *signals* a major change in policy.
His resignation *signaled* trouble at the top.
The company has *signaled* that layoffs are coming.

senses.gloss: To exist as anger or tension that is felt but not openly expressed.
examples: Resentment *simmered* in the office for months.
Tensions have been *simmering* between the two neighbors.
Anger can *simmer* for years before it comes out.

senses.gloss: To pretend to have a feeling or a condition that you do not really have.
examples: He *simulated* surprise when they brought out the cake.
It is hard to *simulate* enthusiasm you don't feel.
She was *simulating* interest in his golf stories.

senses.gloss: To describe something in a general way, without the details.
senses.ru: обрисовывать, обрисовать (в общих чертах); кратко излагать
examples: Let me *sketch* the main idea before we vote.
She *sketched* a rough plan for the summer.
He has *sketched* the outline of a deal, but nothing is signed.

senses.gloss: To remove fat, cream, or foam from the surface of a liquid.
examples: *Skim* the fat off the top of the soup.
She *skimmed* the cream from the milk.
He was *skimming* foam off the stock every few minutes.

senses.gloss: To move quickly and lightly over a surface, almost touching it.
examples: A pelican *skimmed* the surface of the bay.
Swallows *skim* the water at dusk.
The plane was *skimming* the treetops.

senses.gloss: To leave something out, or not do something you would normally do.
examples: I *skipped* breakfast and regretted it by ten.
Don't *skip* your medication.
He has *skipped* class three times this week.

senses.gloss: To bounce something along a surface, or to bounce that way.
senses.ru: пускать блинчики (по воде); подпрыгивать, скакать по поверхности
examples: We used to *skip* stones across the pond.
He *skipped* a flat rock four times.
The ball *skipped* off the pavement and into the street.

senses.gloss: To shut a door or lid violently, with a loud bang.
examples: She *slammed* the door and drove off.
Please don't *slam* the screen door.
He was *slamming* cabinets around the kitchen.

senses.gloss: To criticize someone or something very harshly in public.
examples: Critics *slammed* the movie as lazy and predictable.
The governor has been *slamming* the plan all week.
Reporters will *slam* him for that answer.

senses.gloss: To impose a fine, tax, or penalty on someone, especially suddenly.
examples: Regulators *slapped* the bank with a record fine.
The city will *slap* a fee on plastic bags.
He has been *slapped* with a lawsuit.

senses.gloss: To reduce a price, a budget, or a number of jobs by a large amount.
examples: The store *slashed* prices by half after Christmas.
The company plans to *slash* two hundred jobs.
Funding for the program has been *slashed* again.

senses.gloss: To beat an opponent by a huge margin (informal).
examples: They *slaughtered* us forty-five to three.
We got *slaughtered* in the second half.
Any decent team would *slaughter* us right now.

senses.gloss: To fall to a lower level, or to get slightly worse.
examples: Sales *slipped* three percent last quarter.
His grades have *slipped* since September.
If the ratings *slip* again, the show will be canceled.

senses.gloss: To damage someone's reputation by spreading false or unfair accusations.
examples: The campaign *smeared* his opponent for weeks.
He says he was *smeared* by people who never met him.
They will *smear* anyone who gets in the way.

senses.gloss: To breathe in and out the smoke of a cigarette, a cigar, or a pipe.
examples: He *smokes* about a pack a day.
She *smoked* for twenty years before she quit.
You can't *smoke* inside the building.

senses.gloss: To give off smoke.
examples: The engine was *smoking* by the time we pulled over.
The oil will *smoke* if the pan gets too hot.
The grill *smoked* for a while before it caught.

senses.gloss: To feel strong anger or resentment without showing it openly.
examples: He sat there *smoldering* while she read the letter.
She *smoldered* all the way home.
Resentment can *smolder* for years in a family.

senses.gloss: To make a process easier by removing the problems from it.
examples: A good agent *smooths* the way for first-time buyers.
Her recommendation *smoothed* his path into the program.
They are trying to *smooth* the transition for laid-off workers.

senses.gloss: To give someone so much love and attention that they feel trapped.
examples: She *smothers* her kids and wonders why they don't call.
He felt *smothered* by his family.
Stop *smothering* me; I can do this myself.

senses.gloss: To get or grab something quickly, especially something hard to get (informal).
examples: I *snagged* two tickets before they sold out.
*Snag* a seat near the front if you can.
She has *snagged* an interview with the CEO.

senses.gloss: To say something in a sharp, angry way.
examples: 'Not now,' he *snapped*.
She has been *snapping* at everyone all week.
There's no need to *snap*.

senses.gloss: To take a photograph quickly.
examples: Tourists *snap* pictures of the bridge all day.
She *snapped* a photo before the light changed.
He was *snapping* away with his phone.

senses.gloss: To suddenly lose control of your emotions after a long strain.
senses.ru: срываться, сорваться; не выдерживать, не выдержать
examples: After months of pressure, he finally *snapped*.
She *snapped* and started yelling at the whole room.
Anyone would *snap* under that kind of stress.

senses.gloss: To make something or someone completely wet.
examples: The rain *soaked* us on the way to the car.
A broken pipe was *soaking* the carpet.
One more wave like that will *soak* everything in the boat.

senses.gloss: To rise quickly to a much higher level.
senses.ru: резко расти, взлетать (о ценах, температуре), взлететь
examples: Gas prices *soared* after the storm.
Temperatures will *soar* into the nineties tomorrow.
Costs have been *soaring* all year.

senses.gloss: To train a child or an animal to behave comfortably around others.
examples: Puppies need to be *socialized* early.
The shelter *socializes* every dog before adoption.
We are *socializing* the kitten with our older cat.

senses.gloss: To make an attitude, a tone, or an effect less harsh.
examples: He *softened* his tone when he saw she was crying.
The company has *softened* its stance on remote work.
Nothing can *soften* the blow of losing a job.

senses.gloss: To make a position, an agreement, or support stronger and more definite.
examples: The win *solidified* their lead in the division.
A second meeting should *solidify* the deal.
Support for the bill has *solidified* since the hearings.

senses.gloss: To arrange things in a particular order, such as by date or alphabetically.
examples: *Sort* the list by date and print it.
She *sorted* the emails by sender.
The files are *sorted* alphabetically.

senses.gloss: To make a sound, or to cause something to make a sound as a signal.
examples: The alarm *sounded* at two in the morning.
*Sound* the horn if you see them coming.
A bell was *sounding* somewhere down the street.
